public final class SwiftDataDeckRepository: DeckRepository {
    private let context: ModelContext

    public init(context: ModelContext) {
        self.context = context
    }

    public func fetchAllDecks(includeArchived: Bool) throws -> [Deck] {
        let descriptor: FetchDescriptor<Deck>
        if includeArchived {
            descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Deck>(sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\Deck.createdAt, order: .forward)])
        } else {
            descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Deck>(
                predicate: #Predicate { $0.archivedAt == nil },
                sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\Deck.createdAt, order: .forward)]
            )
        }
        return try context.fetch(descriptor)
    }

    public func createDeck(name: String) throws -> Deck {
        let trimmed = name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: "Deck name must not be empty.")
        }

        let deck = Deck(name: trimmed)
        context.insert(deck)

        do {
            try context.save()
            return deck
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    public func archiveDeck(id: UUID) throws {
        guard let deck = try fetchDeck(id: id) else {
            throw RecallDataError.notFound
        }

        guard deck.archivedAt == nil else { return }
        deck.archivedAt = Date()

        do {
            try context.save()
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    public func deleteDeck(id: UUID) throws {
        guard let deck = try fetchDeck(id: id) else {
            throw RecallDataError.notFound
        }

        context.delete(deck)
        do {
            try context.save()
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    private func fetchDeck(id: UUID) throws -> Deck? {
        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Deck>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.id == id })
        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }
}

public final class SwiftDataCardRepository: CardRepository {
    private let context: ModelContext

    public init(context: ModelContext) {
        self.context = context
    }

    public func create(deckID: UUID, front: String, back: String, note: String?) async throws -> Card {
        try createCardSync(deckID: deckID, front: front, back: back, note: note)
    }

    public func cardsDue(at instant: Date, calendar: Calendar, forDeck: UUID?, includeArchived: Bool) async throws -> [Card] {
        try cardsDueSync(at: instant, calendar: calendar, forDeck: forDeck, includeArchived: includeArchived)
    }

    public func card(forID id: UUID) async throws -> Card? {
        try cardSync(forID: id)
    }

    private func createCardSync(deckID: UUID, front: String, back: String, note: String?) throws -> Card {
        guard let deck = try fetchDeck(id: deckID) else {
            throw RecallDataError.notFound
        }

        let trimmedFront = front.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        let trimmedBack = back.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        guard !trimmedFront.isEmpty, !trimmedBack.isEmpty else {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: "Card front and back must not be empty.")
        }

        let now = Date()
        let card = Card(
            front: trimmedFront,
            back: trimmedBack,
            note: note?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines),
            dueDate: now,
            isDemo: deck.isDemo,
            createdAt: now,
            deck: deck
        )

        context.insert(card)

        do {
            try context.save()
            return card
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    private func cardsDueSync(at instant: Date, calendar: Calendar, forDeck: UUID?, includeArchived: Bool) throws -> [Card] {
        let boundary = SM2Engine.startOfTomorrow(now: instant, calendar: calendar)

        let descriptor: FetchDescriptor<Card>
        if let forDeck {
            descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(
                predicate: #Predicate { card in
                    card.dueDate < boundary &&
                    card.deck?.id == forDeck &&
                    (includeArchived || card.deck?.archivedAt == nil)
                },
                sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\Card.dueDate, order: .forward)]
            )
        } else {
            descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(
                predicate: #Predicate { card in
                    card.dueDate < boundary && (includeArchived || card.deck?.archivedAt == nil)
                },
                sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\Card.dueDate, order: .forward)]
            )
        }

        return try context.fetch(descriptor)
    }

    private func cardSync(forID id: UUID) throws -> Card? {
        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.id == id })
        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }

    private func fetchDeck(id: UUID) throws -> Deck? {
        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Deck>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.id == id })
        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }
}

public final class SwiftDataReviewLogRepository: ReviewLogRepository {
    private let context: ModelContext

    public init(context: ModelContext) {
        self.context = context
    }

    public func append(_ entry: ReviewLogEntry) async throws {
        guard let card = try fetchCard(id: entry.cardId) else {
            throw RecallDataError.notFound
        }

        let reviewLog = ReviewLog(
            timestamp: entry.timestamp,
            grade: entry.grade,
            easeFactorBefore: 0,
            easeFactorAfter: 0,
            intervalBefore: 0,
            intervalAfter: 0,
            repetitionBefore: 0,
            repetitionAfter: 0,
            card: card
        )
        reviewLog.id = entry.id

        context.insert(reviewLog)
        do {
            try context.save()
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    public func history(for cardID: UUID) async throws -> [ReviewLogEntry] {
        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<ReviewLog>(
            predicate: #Predicate { $0.card?.id == cardID },
            sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\ReviewLog.timestamp, order: .forward)]
        )

            return ReviewLogEntry(

                cardId: cardID,
                grade: log.grade,
                timestamp: log.timestamp,
                isDemo: log.card?.isDemo ?? false

    }

    public func deleteByCardID(_ cardID: UUID) async throws {
        let logs = try context.fetch(
            FetchDescriptor<ReviewLog>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.card?.id == cardID })
        )

        for log in logs {
            context.delete(log)
        }

        do {
            try context.save()
        } catch {
            throw RecallDataError.saveFailed(underlying: error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    private func fetchCard(id: UUID) throws -> Card? {
        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Card>(predicate: #Predicate { $0.id == id })
        return try context.fetch(descriptor).first
    }

Manual QA script for a human-run simulator/device session.

Preflight before checking app behavior: use Xcode 16+, iOS 17+ simulator or real device. Install Recall and ensure all accessibility settings in default state. Then run these checks in this exact order so failures are easy to triage.

Initial app and onboarding health check:
- Launch app from a clean install (delete/reinstall once first), keep network on.
- Expected: app starts with a startup loading state, then enters Study tab in a stable state.
- Tap the app root states as needed:
  - If a recovery/error path appears, verify it is readable, actionable, and does not crash on retry.
  - If you ever see blank white screen, no state labels, or repeated spinner forever, stop and capture a screenshot/video because onboarding recovery is broken.

Study tab baseline and deck onboarding:
- From Study, verify deck list empty state.
- Expected: explicit empty-state content (icon + one-line explanation + action to add deck) and no fake data.
- Tap add deck and confirm deck editor opens.
- Enter blank name and attempt save. Expected: save is blocked, and clear validation prevents an empty deck name entry.
- Enter valid deck name and save.
- Expected: deck appears in list, is tappable, and due indicator is coherent (0 due initially).
- Return to deck list and rotate/switch states.
- Expected: no overlapping clipped UI (important to catch broken layout before deeper testing).

Deck and card editing speed/performance checks:
- Open the deck.
- If archive action is present, run both:
  - archive one deck and verify it is marked archived and no longer appears in active review lists.
  - unarchive path if present and verify it returns to normal flow.
- Add first card:
  - Fill front, back, optional note; use keyboard Return/Next flow to avoid taps.
  - Save.
- Expected: keyboard-driven entry is quick and stable; card appears immediately.
- Add second card with same front+back.
- Expected: duplicate handling message appears in CSV/UI workflows where applicable; app should not crash or hang.
- Leave front or back empty and attempt save.
- Expected: validation prevents save and preserves your typed text.
- Delete a card.
- Expected: card is removed; cascade behavior is consistent (review logs tied to that card do not throw visible corruption errors).
- Reopen deck list and confirm counts update instantly and sanely.

Review session due flow:
- Back in Study deck detail, start review.
- If no cards due:
  - Expected: due-absent state is clear and not labeled “error.”
- If cards are due:
  - Tap reveal.
  - Grade through Again → Hard → Good → Easy over at least four cards.
  - Expected: each grade path updates remaining queue immediately, and the same graded card does not reappear as due later in same session.
- Verify non-graded cards remain available.
- Expected: cards still due stay due; graded cards move out.
- On completion:
  - Expected: session summary appears with cards reviewed and again-rate and elapsed time, not before completion.
- Check accessibility for grade controls:
  - Expected: grading is distinguishable without color alone, labels are readable, and buttons are reachable with VoiceOver.
- Run interruption survival manually:
  - Start review with at least two due cards.
  - Grade one card, then force-quit app from the system app switcher while the app is active after save.
  - Reopen and inspect deck list and pending session state.
  - Expected: graded card is not due anymore, only previously ungraded cards remain due. No fabricated session summary should have appeared on relaunch.

Study-all and navigation/session recovery checks:
- Start study-all review with multiple decks.
- Expected: cards are sampled from all due cards and session still enforces interruption safety.

Regression checks that should be re-run after every app mutation:
- Repeat Study → Review → Interrupt → Relaunch at least once per build.
- Repeat Deck edit add/delete paths after every schema-like change.
- Run CSV import/export preview again after any parser update.
- Verify settings actions never claim success before actual completion.
- Verify loading/success/error/empty states are all visible and not replaced by silent fallback text.

- Reminder scheduling service is not fully implemented; reminder settings may currently store user preference without scheduling real notifications.

What would make this phase genuinely remarkable is using this exact checklist as a release gate in a fresh signed build, with mandatory evidence captured for each state transition and each gap, so the product’s transparency promise (“exactly due cards, never fabrication”) is auditable, not assumed.
